_source: Anthropic model catalog via the claude-api skill, checked 2026-08-04. Sonnet 5 list price. The $2/$10 introductory rate through 2026-08-31 is deliberately NOT used, and this is now EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED rather than a precaution: solving the CLI's own per-model costUSD for the implied input rate across three independent run-6/feature cases lands on exactly $3.00/MTok at the 5m cache tier every time, and the $2.00 intro rate would require a cache-write multiplier of 3.8-4.1 when only 1.25 and 2.0 exist. So billing is at list, and the 2026-08-31 expiry moves nothing here. Do not 'correct' Sonnet to $2/$10.
_multipliers_note: Cache tokens dominate input on every real run — the recorded probe has 4 raw input tokens against 71k cache tokens (tests/eval/fixtures/README.md). Pricing input+output alone undercounts a run ~26x. The two cache-write tiers are NOT interchangeable: Claude Code writes 1h entries on the main thread and 5m entries inside subagents, so a single multiplier on the aggregate is wrong for every case that delegates. Verified: with this split, the derived cost reproduces the CLI's own total_cost_usd exactly on both recorded fixtures.
_default_note: Used only when a turn names a model absent from `rates`. Set to the pack's top tier rather than a builder tier because understating cost is the worse failure for a cost instrument. Unknown models are never priced silently — eval-cost.py lists them under `unpriced_models`, and the reconciliation against the CLI's total_cost_usd drifts and says so.
_variants: Model ids in transcripts do not always match these keys, and both known variants came from real runs: a dated full id (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) and a bracketed context variant (`claude-opus-4-8[1m]`, which appears only in the result line's modelUsage ledger). eval-cost.py strips both to find the alias; unresolvable ids are reported, never silently charged at the default rate.
